message.content:
Order filled: 40 shares AAPL at $223.00 (≈$8,920).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided Apple still merits a buy within your mandate. The key figure the task asked for: **Apple's total net sales for fiscal 2024 were $391,035 million**, up 2% from $383,285 million a year earlier, driven by Services growing 13% to $96,169 million and Mac +2%, which offset flat iPhone sales, a 6% decline in iPad, a 7% decline in Wearables/Home/Accessories, and an 8% drop in Greater China. Total gross margin improved to 46.2% (from 44.1%) and operating income rose 7.8% to $123,216 million, with operating cash flow of $118,254 million; net income ($93,736M) and diluted EPS ($6.08) dipped only because of a one-time $10.2 billion net State Aid tax charge that pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — an after-tax, non-operating item rather than a deterioration in the business. The balance sheet shows $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities and a fresh $110 billion buyback authorization (Apple repurchased ~112 million shares at roughly $221–224 during the September quarter), which supports the stock. With the quote at $222.70 (bid/ask $222.68/$222.72), I placed one buy order for **40 shares at a $223.00 limit**, a limit about 0.13% above the market, for roughly $8,920 — inside your $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance, with no money moved out of the account.
